generated_by: tools/vectors-gen (deterministic; do not edit by hand)
description: Assertion sequences a conforming node MUST reject. §4.3: "Any assertion violating this table is invalid and MUST be discarded." These cases are the operative definition of M-14 — a verifier that accepts any of them is non-conforming.

cases.name: owner-backdates-to-manufacture-an-elapsed-acceptance-window
cases.description: §4.3 (v0.2, #38): the attack the monotonic rule exists for. Both windows in this spec are measured between two `asserted_at` values written by the SAME party, so an owner could mint evidence dated far in the past and a closure dated now, and a node computing the window from those two timestamps would find it elapsed — on an edge the counterparty had only ever confirmed. Nothing about the transition is illegal; the timestamps are the lie.

cases.name: counterparty-backdates-a-dispute
cases.description: §4.3 (v0.2, #38): the same shape on the other side. A backdated `disputed` would start the dispute window in the past and let the disputant assert `expired` immediately.

cases.name: proposed-by-owed-to
cases.description: M-1: you cannot propose someone else’s promise. Only the owner may sign `proposed`.

cases.name: owner-self-confirms
cases.description: M-2: the counterparty’s signature is what makes the edge exist. An owner confirming their own proposal is the single most damaging forgery the table has to stop.

cases.name: confirmed-by-third-party
cases.description: M-3: edges are strictly two-party; a non-party signature is never valid.

cases.name: closed-without-confirmation
cases.description: M-2: an unconfirmed proposal is not a promise and cannot be closed straight out of `proposed`.

cases.name: on-evidence-closed-by-owed-to
cases.description: §4.4: under on-evidence only the owner may close.

cases.name: closed-without-evidence-hash
cases.description: §4.4: closure under on-evidence requires a non-null evidence_hash. "The system has an opinion only where it has evidence."

cases.name: released-by-owner
cases.description: §4.3: release is forgiveness by the creditor. An owner releasing themselves would let anyone discharge their own debt.

cases.name: expired-with-null-due
cases.description: §4.3: expiry requires a non-null due. Undated commitments MUST NOT time-escalate.

cases.name: expired-before-due
cases.description: §4.3: expiry may only be asserted after due.

cases.name: dispute-expiry-before-the-window-elapsed
cases.description: §4.4: the dispute window is what stops `expired` becoming a way to walk away from a dispute the moment it is raised. Expiring early would hand the disputed party a unilateral exit — the mirror of the freeze the window exists to prevent.

cases.name: dispute-expiry-by-a-non-party
cases.description: §4.4 says EITHER PARTY, and a stranger is neither. The window makes the timing public, so without this an onlooker could end an edge simply by waiting for it.

cases.name: disputed-without-evidence
cases.description: §4.3: evidence_hash is REQUIRED on a dispute.

cases.name: tacit-close-before-window-elapsed
cases.description: §4.4: the owner may only record tacit acceptance AFTER the acceptance window expires. Closing early would let the owner manufacture acceptance the counterparty never gave.

cases.name: forged-signature
cases.description: A well-formed but non-verifying signature MUST be discarded.

cases.name: signature-attributed-to-other-party
cases.description: Assertion claims by=owed_to but is signed with the owner’s key. Verifying `sig` against `by` is what stops a party from fabricating the counterparty’s confirmation.

cases.name: explicit-open-assertion
cases.description: §4.3: the confirmed → open transition is implicit and no row authorizes any signer to produce it, so an assertion whose `state` is `open` violates the table and MUST be discarded under M-14. Normative as of v0.1-pre; formerly an interpretation.

cases.name: replayed-confirmation
cases.description: Re-submitting `confirmed` on an already-open edge has no legal source state.

cases.name: assertion-after-terminal-state
cases.description: Once released, the edge is closed to further assertions.

cases.name: edge-id-mismatch
cases.description: An assertion naming a different edge MUST NOT be applied to this chain.

cases.name: superseded-by-third-party
cases.description: §4.5: supersession requires both parties of the OLD edge — not an outside key.

cases.name: supersession-double-signed-by-one-party
cases.description: §4.5: the owner signing `superseded` twice must not substitute for the counterparty’s signature.

cases.name: on-acceptance-edge-with-null-window
cases.description: §4.1: acceptance_window MUST be non-null iff closure_policy is on-acceptance, and there is no default. A null window on an on-acceptance edge is malformed and the edge accepts no assertions at all — treating null as "no window" would let the owner record tacit acceptance instantly, which is the exact forgery §4.4 exists to prevent.

cases.name: on-evidence-edge-with-non-null-window
cases.description: §4.1, the other direction: an acceptance_window on an on-evidence edge is meaningless and MUST be null. A verifier that tolerates it accepts an edge whose closure rule and closure timing disagree about which policy is in force.
